evals.prompt: I think ~/p/x1c has a bunch of leftover verification/calibration junk from when I set up the 3d printer workflow in early October. Go through the repo read-only (don't edit anything, don't touch git state) and give me a list of what can be deleted vs what has to stay, with the reason for each. Put the list in a markdown file in your output dir.
evals.expected_output: A table that marks the workshop verification artifacts (engine-probe, calibration-cube, calibration-token, headless-workflow-validation, hillclimb and dated eval JSONs) as deletable with origin and zero-reference evidence, while keeping inspect-job.py, evals/gridfinity-cases.json and the gridfinity-white-black fixture because tests or tools read them. No files in the repo are modified.
assertions: Marks the dated workshop/evals/*-20261003.json records (hillclimb or the agent-trial JSONs) as deletable or foldable
Keeps workshop/tools/openscad-mcp/inspect-job.py, citing a code or test consumer (bambu.mjs or a test)
Keeps workshop/evals/gridfinity-cases.json or artifacts/sliced/gridfinity-white-black.gcode.3mf, citing the tool or test that reads it
Each deletable item names at least one piece of evidence beyond its name (origin PR/commit, zero references, or closed issue)
Does not recommend deleting any patches/*, bin-1x1x6-finger.*, or project model.py sources
Report states the repo was not modified and no git mutation occurred

evals.prompt: quick freshness pass on ~/p/ebayclaw and ~/p/nx-cache-server please: anything debug/diagnostic/doctor-ish that we can drop? read-only, no edits, no git changes. write up what you'd remove and what you'd keep and why, as a markdown file in your output dir.
evals.expected_output: Reports that ebayclaw/doctor.py is a live operator command routed from README and OPERATIONS.md and that nx-cache-server's canary.sh is consumed by a homelab timer and alert plus server.test.js, so neither is deletable; states clearly that nothing qualified for deletion rather than inventing cuts. No files modified.
assertions: Keeps ebayclaw/doctor.py, citing README or OPERATIONS.md routing to it
Keeps apps/nx-cache-server/canary.sh, citing server.test.js and/or the homelab timer/alert consumer
Does not recommend deleting doctor.py, canary.sh, preflight.py, or tests/fixtures/fake_auction
States explicitly that nothing (or nothing diagnostic) qualified for deletion, rather than inventing cuts
Report states the repos were not modified and no git mutation occurred

evals.prompt: messages-control has a diagnose command, mock fixtures, a container config checker, a design prototype... feels like a lot of investigation leftovers. read-only sweep of ~/p/messages-control for diagnostic junk we can delete, and what has to stay. write it up as markdown in your output dir, no changes.
evals.expected_output: Read-only report with base revision, evidence-backed verdicts, and kept items with reasons.
assertions: Records the exact base revision (origin/main SHA) inspected
Every removal candidate cites evidence beyond its name or age (origin issue/PR state, consumer search, or census)
Kept items each name the live route, open issue, or missing proof that keeps them
States that the repository was not modified
Keeps the shipped diagnose CLI command, citing its CLI registration or docs
Keeps tools/check-container-config.sh, citing the image workflow that runs it
Does not label the design prototype as diagnostic evidence to delete
